No guard, default or earlier branch rescues the path: train_instruct.py has no post-train() fallback copy, submission_dir is only ever written by _on_save_body, and the commit's own six tests check in-memory state only, never the disk outcome. Two corrections to the finder's trigger, one down and one up. Down: the instruct eval batch is 1 (instruct_config.py:224 '--per_device_eval_batch_size 1'), not 4, and kl_per_token_chunked bounds fp32 temporaries to 512 MB, so the '11 GiB per tensor' OOM is overstated by ~4x and is not the deterministic trigger claimed. That full-FT + KL-wired state is exactly what 4d1d8c7 (same audited range) now produces on the legacy cascade: instruct_config.py buckets below 9B are use_lora False, and resolve_kl_for_request reads USE_KL=1 from the environment there. So on a KL-flagged instruct task (~20% of them) whose adaptive planner crashes or fails its sanity check, HEAD ships a noised base model where the pre-d1ec63a code shipped the step-500 checkpoint trained on the task. Severity stays high: it is a forfeit-equivalent (bottom-two) on a reachable, deterministic path, but conditional on a compound precondition and not a crash.

votes.verdict: NOT refuted — the defect reproduces with the real callback and is reachable from train_instruct, but via a different trigger than the finding states. The finding's OOM trigger (eval batch 4, 11 GiB logits, gemma-2-2b LoRA path) is wrong on the numbers: both config paths emit --per_device_eval_batch_size 1 (instruct_config.py:224, reused by adaptive_config.py:2922-2930) and kl_per_token_chunked bounds the fp32 temporaries, so at batch 1 the metric is cheaper than a KL training step that is already succeeding; an OOM on EVERY eval is not constructible on the default adaptive path, and a transient one leaves later evals finite so promotion happens. The deterministic, reachable trigger is the legacy config cascade (ADAPTIVE_MODE=0 / adaptive crash / sanity fail, text_trainer.py:1063-1120) on a KL-flagged task with a model < 9B: every legacy instruct bucket below 9B has use_lora=False (verified: 2.61B -> 2_4_b use_lora=False), commit 4d1d8c7 (in range) now resolves USE_KL=1 from the env on that path and wires _kl_metric (train_instruct.py:711-740), a non-PEFT model exposes no disable_adapter (verified None on transformers 4.51.3), so _kl_metric raises RuntimeError at train_instruct.py:717 on every call before any forward -> compute_loss returns inf on every eval -> on_evaluate (customized_trainer.py:778) returns unranked every time -> nothing promoted, _wsm_last_eval_step never set, has_checkpoint set unconditionally at :1176 so the end_time branch at :613 does not fall to save-only, and the :625 save-only guard only fires when remaining < cost while the lead is sized to 1.25*cycle+45s so the eval is admitted -> submission_dir never created -> text_trainer.py:1417 'Training failed' -> add_random_noise at :1500. Meanwhile the KL mixin is fail-soft on the same missing disable_adapter (kl_trainer_mixin.py:60-63), so training runs normally and produces good plain-CE checkpoints, none of which ship. Before 4d1d8c7 this path had KL off and shipped the best plain-CE checkpoint; the interaction of d1ec63a + 4d1d8c7 turns the legacy safety net — whose stated purpose is 'a vanilla submission instead of no submission at all' — into a noise submission on every KL-flagged task it catches. Severity kept at high rather than critical: it loses the submission, but only on the fallback config path (which has fired in a real tournament before, 2026-05-22) combined with the ~20% of instruct tasks that are KL-flagged; the default adaptive path forces LoRA on KL tasks (param_count defaults to 1B when unknown, so the use_lora=False-on-None branch is unreachable there). Suggested fix shape: on the legacy path force LoRA when USE_KL=1 (mirror _select_lora_config), or make the trainer ship the last/best-CE checkpoint when every eval was unranked instead of nothing.

confirmed.scenario: Boss-round guaranteed 35-71B instruct task, e.g. Qwen3-32B-class (h=5120, 64 layers, vocab 152k) on 3x H200 (the validator's H100->H200 conversion). Adaptive: estimate_max_batch_size -> ~15, multi-GPU cap (param>=9e9) -> batch 4, max_length 2048, LoRA, ds, gradient_checkpointing False. Saved activations without checkpointing ~34*h*layers*tokens = 34*5120*64*8192 tokens ≈ 91 GB per rank, plus ZeRO-3 partition 21 GB, gathered layer, fp32 logits upcast 4x2048x152k ≈ 7.5 GB -> ~121 GB of 141 GB before allocator reserve; a 40B/h=8192/60-layer model reaches ~137 GB of activations alone -> torch.OutOfMemoryError on the first forward. The OOM ladder then halves batch 4->2->1, each rung re-paying a 35-70B ZeRO-3 load inside the task's own hours_to_complete; at batch 1 the ladder cannot halve further and moves to max_length. Net: the change converts a working 35-71B shape into 1-3 relaunches on the round that guarantees this task, in exchange for no measured benefit.

votes.verdict:
The finding's MECHANISM survives but its SCENARIO is wrong on three counts, and the reachable path is a different guard than the one it cites.

REFUTED parts: (1) The headline max_step / EXPT_BUDGET_CAP=1 scenario is unreachable. After the step-500 cycle is measured at 470 s the lead is widened to 11 min, so WhenToEvalHandler returns reason="end_time" at the first step with <660 s left (step 742 in the simulation, 658 s remaining), the guard sees 658 >= 470 and runs a FULL eval, then sets should_training_stop — step 862 is never reached. Nothing "deterministic on every capped run". (2) The periodic/epoch/max_step guard the finding quotes (customized_trainer.py:640-653) cannot refuse while an eval-selected best is on disk: an evaluated best implies a measured cycle C, which widens the lead to >=1.25C+45 s, and end_time is checked every step, so that guard can only fire if the single previous step took longer than lead*60-C = 190 s (gemma-2-2b), 161 s (gate instruct). When it does fire (estimate regime, no cycle measured yet) there is no evaluated best to lose — exactly the step-149-of-150 case in be81e18. (3) "a probe-run best already sits in submission_dir": probe runs set should_save=False and save_strategy="no" (customized_trainer.py:517-521, 580-582) and never write submission_dir; and the final run's first eval always promotes (best_checkpoint_info is None, line 800), so a leftover would be overwritten by design anyway.

SURVIVING defect (reproduced in the pinned venv, default path, no env opt-in, instruct/KL-instruct/DPO/LoRA or full, rank 0 does the copy under ZeRO-3 too): the END_TIME guard from 68083c2 (customized_trainer.py:620-631) routes into the same save_only branch (lines 1181-1220) with has_checkpoint=True and an eval-selected best in submission_dir. Whenever a periodic/epoch eval is triggered with remaining time R in [lead*60, 2C+step) — for the real gemma-2-2b task (C=470 s, lead 11 min) that is a ~280 s window in front of every periodic trigger (500, 1000, 1500…) — the cycle itself consumes the remaining budget, the next step trips end_time with remaining < C, the eval is refused, and _on_save_body rmtree's submission_dir, copytree's the current unevaluated checkpoint-(S+1) and writes loss.txt "S+1,proxy=no_eval". best_checkpoint_info still names the old best but has no consumer outside customized_trainer.py; on_train_end only does the WSM merge, whose rollback target is whatever is in submission_dir; dev_absorption._prior_dev_loss then reads "proxy=" and disarms its too-hot guard (a97c063). This contradicts be81e18's own message that proxy=no_eval is "Only reachable when the run ends before periodic_save_steps (500) is ever hit". The existing test test_at_the_trigger_an_eval_that_cannot_finish_is_skipped stops at `cb.save_only is True` and never calls on_save, so the artefact outcome is unasserted. Harm is real only when the last periodic eval did NOT improve on the best (drift/overfit — the case the early-stop machinery exists for); on a monotone run checkpoint-(S+1) ~= the just-promoted checkpoint-S. Note the pre-range code on this exact timeline would have started a 470 s eval with ~328 s left and been killed by the validator, so the guard is a net improvement; the residual bug is that the refused save overwrites an evaluated best instead of leaving it in place. Severity stays medium: silent quality loss, but only on the (timing window) x (non-improving last eval) intersection, not a crash and not every run.

NOT reachable as the finder wrote it: the instruct command template pins --per_device_eval_batch_size 1 (scripts/instruct_config.py:224) while the train batch is >= 1, dev rows are bounded by the same max_length as train rows (train_instruct.py:291-300, utility.py:91), and eval runs under torch.no_grad(); a reference forward that survives training steps (B>=1 rows with autograd activations resident) does not OOM on a single no-grad dev row, so 'eval batches OOM, training steps do not' cannot be sized from the batch settings. The REACHABLE direction is the reverse, and it is the exact case the gate's 'KL term failed' check exists for: a genuine training-side reference-forward OOM is caught and _kl_disabled_reason is set; at the next eval cycle the 1-row no-grad reference forward succeeds, an EVAL batch prints 'KL term recovered after N CE-only step(s)', clears _kl_disabled_reason and sets _kl_last (so the eval log line carries a kl value); the next training step OOMs again and prints a second 'KL term failed'. One continuous training outage reads as k+1 outages with k recoveries, which is precisely the reading aecb7c0 says it exists to prevent ('instead of leaving KL term failed at step N to be read against a log that later shows kl values again'). This shape was already observed on the gate 2026-09-13 ('recovered after 2000 CE-only step(s)' then 'KL term failed 2 time(s)', tests/test_liger_is_decided_by_liger.py:112-120); that trigger (liger) is closed by ae8a208, but a memory-driven training-side OOM reproduces it with no liger involved. Impact is bounded: the gate fails on any count >= 1 so its verdict is unchanged (only the count is inflated by one per eval cycle), and _kl_off_steps stays accurate because successful eval batches do not increment it and failed ones only add to a count that is already non-zero in the one-sided case. So: a real unguarded instrument, severity low as the finder had it, with the scenario corrected from 'fake outage' to 'fake recovery'.

The mechanism is real and reproduces in the pinned venv (transformers 4.51.3 prediction_step calls self.compute_loss; the mixin's compute_loss runs on every eval batch with model.training == False; nothing guards the counter, so a forced eval-only exception yields _kl_off_steps=5 after a 5-row evaluate(), a 'KL term failed' line, and 'recovered after 5 CE-only step(s)' on the next training step). But the scenario's trigger cannot be built on any real entry point. The finding needs an exception that fires on eval batches and NOT on training micro-batches, and its stated cause is 'eval batch larger than train batch'. On the only path that instantiates the mixin (train_instruct.py:585-600; train_dpo/train_grpo never import it) the command template pins `--per_device_eval_batch_size 1` (scripts/instruct_config.py:224) and adaptive_config reuses that same get_run_cmd (adaptive_config.py:2922-2930); the OOM ladder only lowers the train batch, never raises eval; train and dev rows are padded/truncated with one max_length (utility.py:91). Eval runs under model.eval()+torch.no_grad() with no autograd graph, while a training micro-batch at B>=1 additionally holds the fp32 CE upcast, the logits grad and the log_softmax intermediates of the KL term — so eval per-batch memory is strictly below the training peak and an eval-only OOM at batch 1 is not constructible; an exception that fires in eval also fires on every training micro-step, where the count is the intended signal. The one real-world conflation of eval and train steps by this instrument was the REVERSE direction (liger's fused CE drops logits only in training mode: gate run 03d3a5a printed 'recovered after 2000 CE-only step(s)' on an eval prediction step, then 'KL term failed' again), recorded at model_utility.py:66-75 and closed in-range by ae8a208 (use_kl -> liger refused). The stringify-before-filter ordering also predates ec732ed (unchanged context lines in the diff), so the commit did not introduce it; its docstring describes is_poor_item in isolation correctly. The mechanism is real at unit level but the scenario is unreachable from any real entry point. The legacy GRPO buckets that do this at 20-40B also set use_4bit=True and use_vllm=False; adaptive's GRPO branch does not appear to set use_4bit. Whether a 20-40B LoRA GRPO under plain DDP fits on 3-5x H200 is not something I could size without the vLLM colocate numbers; the 'Qwen3-32B trains fine' memory item does not record which config it ran under.

[adaptive-config] estimate_max_batch_size (dynamics_utils.py:939-973) returns 1 whenever bf16 weights exceed 0.75x one card's free VRAM, with no ZeRO-3 awareness — so every 40-71B ds run plans batch 1 x grad_accum 4 (effective 32 on 8 ranks). Pre-existing, but 1728a0d's checkpointing-off shape now rides on top of it; batch 1 without checkpointing at max_length 4096 on a 70B/h=8192/80-layer model is ~91 GB of activations + 28 GB partition on H200 — fits on paper, no margin measured.

[adaptive-config] count_params_from_safetensors is fixed, but count_params_from_bin (the next rung in get_model_size_from_local_path) still torch.load()s every shard; a .bin-only 35-71B repo on the legacy cascade would hit the same SIGKILL the commit describes. I could not name a pool model at that size that ships only .bin, so no scenario.

[adaptive-config] dpo_batch_ceiling's headline number (24 on the smoke run, predicted peak 58.3 of 79.11 GiB with 15.6 GiB reserved-but-unallocated observed at OOM) is stated by the commit as 'from the GPU run that follows' — i.e. the ceiling itself has not been measured to fit; the ladder only proved 17 fits and 35 does not.

[adaptive-config] count_params_from_safetensors now returns a finite undercount when one shard header fails to parse (skip-and-continue), bypassing the regex fallback that would otherwise read the size from the model name; on an anonymised task the old path crashed (None < int) so this is not worse, but a partial count can land a model in the wrong legacy bucket rather than failing loudly.

[shim-and-loading] Whether train_instruct actually trains a Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration wrapper end-to-end on 4.51.3 (forward without pixel_values, liger's multimodal gemma3 patch, chat template) — the medium gemma3 finding assumes the load succeeds and training runs; if the wrapper crashes elsewhere first the finding degrades to 'docstring premise false, no quality effect'.

[shim-and-loading] trl 0.18.0 GRPOTrainer under ZeRO-3/FSDP reloads its reference with `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model.config._name_or_path, **model_init_kwargs)` — unshimmed rope and fp32 (no torch_dtype). Dormant only because 1728a0d routes GRPO to ddp at every size; if that decision is ever reversed the KL reference is mis-encoded. DPO's ZeRO-3 reference is a deepcopy and inherits the shim.

[shim-and-loading] count_params_from_safetensors (model_utility.py:126) sums every *.safetensors in the directory; a repo that ships both consolidated.safetensors and model-0000N shards (Mistral-style) is counted twice and routed to the wrong size bucket. Pre-existing behaviour (the old load_file loop did the same), not introduced in this range, so not filed.

[shim-and-loading] The dtype -> torch_dtype non-mapping was checked at all seven load sites (train_instruct x2, train_dpo x2, train_grpo, dev_absorption, dynamics_utils, score_against_leaderboard): every one passes torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 explicitly, so it is a recorded decision with no reachable fp32 load — except the dormant TRL ZeRO-3 GRPO reference reload above.

[shim-and-loading] MiniCPM5-1B / llama-typed configs with rope_type 'longrope' inside rope_parameters: 4.51.3's llama longrope path ignores original_max_position_embeddings inside the dict when the config class lacks the attribute, so the short/long factor switch is decided on max_position_embeddings. Same behaviour as an upstream 4.x-shaped file, so not shim-specific; not filed.

[shim-and-loading] monkeypatch.py's +22 is the PackedDataset tail-truncation, not a runtime patch: it runs once per PackedDataset construction (train_ds only, dev_ds is not packed) and each ladder relaunch is a fresh process, so it cannot double-apply; liger's monkey patches are module-level function reassignments and re-applying them on the LRRT reload (train_instruct.py:780) is idempotent. No finding.

[trainer-and-fallback] customized_trainer.py:1181-1216 — the save_only branch runs BEFORE the best-checkpoint branch and unconditionally rmtree's submission_dir and copies the CURRENT checkpoint with loss.txt 'proxy=no_eval' (non-GRPO: _h3_last_proxy is None). This week's guards (68083c2 end_time, 08b0337 periodic/epoch) make save_only reachable with an eval-selected best already in submission_dir, so a refused trigger replaces a measured best with an unmeasured checkpoint and disarms the dev-absorption guard. After a cycle has been measured the lead is 1.25C+45s, so a post-measurement refusal needs a single step longer than ~0.25C+45s (2+ min) between the handler's check and the trigger; I could not name a 1-GPU instruct/DPO shape where that happens, so it is listed here rather than as a finding. Pre-measurement it is subsumed by finding 1.

[trainer-and-fallback] text_trainer.halve_request_max_length keys the DPO rung on the PLANNER's max_length (8f1bc00 says 1024 while DPO trains at min(max_position_embeddings,4096)=2048): a DPO task whose planner max_length is <=512 gets 'max_length already at floor' and the rung never fires although DPO could still halve 2048; and when it does fire it drops DPO from 2048 to 512 in one rung. Pre-existing (f322437), not introduced in the range.

[trainer-and-fallback] add_random_noise._skip decides 'a safetensors set exists' per directory from any *.safetensors name; a base directory holding a stray/partial safetensors file alongside a complete pytorch_model.bin set would ship the safetensors and drop the .bin. I could not name a real G.O.D pool repo with that layout, so no scenario.

[data-and-objective] kl_trainer_mixin / train_instruct (pre-existing, 008c10a, outside the range): compute_loss also runs during evaluation, so on a LoRA KL run eval_loss already contains kl_coef*KL(batch) and the callback's compute_loss adds kl_coef*KL(dev) again — the checkpoint is selected on CE + ~2*coef*KL. Not introduced by 7ecde1c..8f1bc00, so not filed; worth a separate look.

[data-and-objective] dev_absorption too-hot guard vs KL tasks (pre-existing, a915383/008c10a): on a KL-instruct run loss.txt holds the weighted metric (CE + coef*KL), while the absorption pass measures plain CE, so `prior` is inflated and the guard is looser than the 28c9f3bb calibration assumed. Both sides predate the range.

[data-and-objective] dedup_knn Jaccard stage (opt-in, INSTRUCT_DEDUP_JACCARD unset everywhere in scripts/ops/dockerfiles): the comment at :139-142 claims the shared rule stops the constant-instruction collapse, but with a long constant instruction and short inputs the char-5-gram Jaccard is still ~|instr|/(|instr|+2|input|) > 0.85 and every row would collapse; toy showed the stage also drops same-prompt/different-output rows. Unreachable in production today.

[data-and-objective] dev_absorption RESERVE_SECONDS=90 (882c0c5, pre-range): the clock check runs only inside the loop; copytree of the full submission plus save_pretrained after the loop is unbudgeted. Fine for <=5B bf16 on NVMe, unmeasured for the gpt-oss `use_lora=False` override (instruct_config.py:400) where the plain from_pretrained + AdamW would also OOM a single GPU before opt.step(). Pre-existing.

[data-and-objective] dev_absorption merged-LoRA question: no merge_and_unload path exists in train_instruct/train_dpo/train_grpo — every use_lora submission is the raw checkpoint-N adapter directory (customized_trainer on_save copytree), so _is_adapter_submission fires on all of them and a merged LoRA (no adapter_config.json) cannot arise from this code; the absorbed pass's loss is NOT written back to loss.txt (copytree keeps the original), so a second absorption or the WSM gate cannot misread it.

[data-and-objective] dedup 2deaebc: the exact-stage key now joins all populated prompt fields and keeps the first output; leak_key groups the same fields normalised, so rows identical on prompt with different outputs survive dedup and share a bucket — no new dev/train leak and no new train-set shrink found. The hardcoded key list still ignores non-standard field names (a `query`/`text` prompt column with an `answer` output collapses rows by answer), but that predates the range.

[smoke-ops] ab_rope_20260913: the pre-shim arm's own dev loss.txt (704,0.7988752) matches the shim arm's 5.12.1 held-out mean (0.7989080, v512_lostinjamal.json) to four decimals. The per-example vectors differ, so this is probably coincidence, but the file labelling of the two v512_* vectors is worth a second look before +0.159 nats is cited again.

[smoke-ops] The runbook's step-2 loop failed on the box (`fatal: cannot change to '/root/lostinjamal-preshim'`, ab_rope.out:1) and the pre-shim arm was re-run separately under tag rope-preshim; neither the cause nor the substitute command is recorded in the runbook or RESULT.md.

[smoke-ops] deadline_instruct_20260914.md says the box holds dd558022 "plus three others (23:25–23:40)"; the gate's dpo/grpo/chat paths write exactly three synthetic *_train_data.json files, so those three may be smoke fixtures rather than real tasks — which would also make the gate's abort listing (finding 3) the source of that count.

[smoke-ops] score_against_leaderboard.py's fixed LoRA route (`from_pretrained(<adapter dir>, rope_theta=…)`) has only been executed on CPU here with a tiny Llama + peft adapter; the banked local numbers in RESULT.md are all from the pre-fix scorer, so the fixed scorer has not been run on the real arms.

[wires] config_shim.legacy_rope_kwargs hands `rope_theta` to from_pretrained whenever a 5.x-written config carries `rope_parameters`; on a rotary model whose 4.51.3 config class has NO rope_theta attribute (GPTJConfig, CodeGenConfig) the kwarg falls through AutoConfig as unused and reaches `GPTJForCausalLM.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'rope_theta'` — reproduced on the pinned venv with a synthetic dir (scratchpad t_unused.py). This would crash every load site (train_instruct both loaders, train_dpo, train_grpo; absorption/dynamics catch it) -> not OOM -> retries repeat -> base-model fallback. UNVERIFIED premise: whether transformers 5.12.1 actually writes rope_parameters for gpt_j/codegen and whether any pool model has that model_type; no 5.x install is available locally to check.

[wires] dpo_batch_ceiling multiplies `vram_available_gb` by 1024**3 — if measure_gpu reports decimal GB the free-VRAM input is ~7% optimistic; inside the 0.75 safety factor, could not build a failing scenario without the GPU sensor's units.

[wires] `_model_gib` in on_train_begin counts the full frozen base on a LoRA run, but the copy term the envelope is meant to cover is only the adapter on that path; this contributes to the 8B over-prediction in finding 1 and is folded there rather than reported separately.

[wires] GRPOCustomEvalSaveCallback is constructed without `end_time=`/`checking_mode=` (train_grpo.py:514-523, pre-existing), so `_seconds_to_end_time()` returns None and the new guards are inert on GRPO while on_train_begin still prints a '[deadline] a full eval cycle is estimated' line — misleading log only, no behavioural scenario.

[wires] 8f1bc00's DPO ceiling has never been executed on a GPU per its own message ('The 24 itself, and the measured peak at 24, come from the GPU run that follows'); the ladder still covers an over-estimate, so no failure scenario, but the constant is unmeasured on the box it targets.
[wires] The [vram] print in on_train_end reads get_device_properties(0) rather than LOCAL_RANK — cosmetic on homogeneous boxes; not a finding.

[oom-and-resources] resolve_distributed_shape routes GRPO to ddp at every size: a >9e9 GRPO model on 2-8 H100s would hold full bf16 weights per rank beside vLLM colocate (a 32B = 64 GB/rank) and OOM at load through the whole ladder; the boss ships the same shape and no GRPO task above ~8B (cd6788e7 is Llama-3-8b) is in the recon set, so no scenario with a real task could be built.

[oom-and-resources] count_params_from_safetensors now skips an unreadable shard and returns the partial sum ('a finite count still routes the run'); a 70B with one corrupt shard header would be routed as a ~60B and still fit ds, but I could not find a case where the under-count crosses the 9e9 ds/ddp threshold or a 1-GPU bucket boundary.

[oom-and-resources] add_random_noise._skip hides every .bin/.pth/.pt when ANY *.safetensors sits in the directory; a base repo whose safetensors set is partial beside a complete .bin set would ship an unloadable fallback, but no such repo is in the pool as far as the recon shows.

[oom-and-resources] The envelope's K constants were fitted from cycles recorded with EMIT_PER_EXAMPLE_LOSSES=1 (gate exports it; the real 59469903 cycle predates the default-off flip) while tournaments run with it off, so every estimate is 2-5x above the HEAD cycle even inside the fitted range; folded into finding 1 as evidence rather than reported alone because the direction is 'refuse', and on the 59469903 timeline itself (step 500 with 775 s left vs 623 s estimated) the eval still runs.

[oom-and-resources] delete_poor_checkpoints now keeps every output_dir whose probe has no finite loss instead of raising; probe runs set should_save=False so the retained directories are normally empty, but a probe that evaluated (steps_per_epoch <= checking_step=80) and then failed its held-out eval keeps a full checkpoint per attempt on /app.

[oom-and-resources] measure_gpu (pre-existing, called by the adaptive planner inside the text_trainer parent) opens a CUDA context on GPU 0 that persists for the whole training subprocess; not in the range, noted because fit_grpo_generations adds another torch.cuda call in that parent (device_count, context-free).
